title: Mikhail Tal!
transcript: Brilliancy, genius and style, the magician of Riga, Mikhail Tal, brought all of these things as he dominated the chess world some 70 years ago, becoming the eighth world chess champion. During a time where the Russian school of chess was trying to find a solution to chess and approach it in a scientific way, Mikhail Tal was playing his own style of chess and making true magic happen over the board. This game happened in 1969. Mikhail Tal is playing with the white pieces and he decides to start with an attack on the king's side after g5, opening up this side of the board. Black correctly trades the rooks and now any usual player would simply take the rook back, having a lot of pressure and being better in this position. But this would take a while to convert into a won game and that is not the style of chess that Mikhail Tal used to play. And in this position, he decides to leave the rook there and take the knight on f6 instead, a move that shocked the audience of the time. This seems to simply hang the other rook with a temp on the queen. You have to take the rook or you're going to lose your queen on the next move. But if you do that, now black has a chance to capture back the pawn and now white would have a knight for rook and would have lost a pawn, being in a lost position. But Tal had calculated one of the most incredible sequences of the last century and he decides to capture back the rook with the knight, now opening up a Mexican standoff between the queens. Of course, if black takes now this pawn, they would lose the queen and the game. But of course, they can take the queen themselves and now after the bishop takes, again, you would lose this pawn and we would have the same situation. Black is up material, which is exactly why the magician of Riga ignores the queen and takes the bishop, a beautiful move, understanding the fact that this is a checkmate threat in one move once we get a new queen and the black queen is still hanging. Black has no way to cover both threats at the same time. The king cannot approach the pawn, and so it tries to run this way. Now, white promotes to a queen, and after the black king moves, it desperado sacrifices the queen for the rook, and now picks up the queen. And in this position, black resigned the game. Follow for more.
